name: Pyramids of Giza

stages.note: Workers are building the Great Pyramid for the pharaoh Khufu.
The pyramids shine with smooth white limestone casing.
Most of the casing stones were taken in the 1300s to build Cairo.
Today the site is protected, and the pyramids are surrounded by the city.

fact: The Great Pyramid of Khufu, finished around 2560 BCE, was the tallest human-made structure in the world for over 3,800 years.
facts: The pyramids were built by organised teams of workers who were fed and housed in a nearby town.
The Great Sphinx has the body of a lion and the head of a king.
Khafre's pyramid still has some of its original casing stones near the top.

name: Lighthouse of Alexandria

stages.note: The Pharos lighthouse guides ships into Alexandria with fire and polished mirrors.
Earthquakes badly damaged the lighthouse.
A citadel was built on the site using some of its stones.

fact: The Lighthouse of Alexandria, about 100 m tall, was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
facts: It was built on the island of Pharos, which gave its name to lighthouses in several languages.

name: Petra — the Treasury

stages.note: Petra is the bustling capital of the Nabataeans, a trading people.
Petra has been mostly abandoned.
Petra is a World Heritage Site visited by people from all over the world.

fact: Petra, in Jordan, is a city carved into rose-coloured sandstone cliffs by the Nabataeans more than 2,000 years ago.
facts: The Nabataeans built clever channels and cisterns to collect water in the desert.

name: Persepolis

stages.note: Persepolis is a grand ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Persian Empire.
Persepolis was destroyed by fire in 330 BCE. Its columns and carvings still stand among the ruins.

fact: Persepolis was the ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Persian Empire, famous for its staircases carved with people bringing gifts from across the empire.

name: Ziggurat of Ur

stages.note: The ziggurat towers over the city of Ur, with a temple at its top.
The lower terrace's facade was partly reconstructed.

fact: The Great Ziggurat of Ur was built about 4,100 years ago from mud bricks, with a core of sun-dried brick and an outer layer of baked brick set in bitumen.

name: Hagia Sophia

stages.note: Its giant dome seems to float above a ring of windows.

fact: Hagia Sophia in Istanbul was completed in 537. Its huge dome was an engineering marvel, and it was the world's largest cathedral for nearly a thousand years.
facts: Minarets were added after 1453, when the building became a mosque.

name: Abu Simbel temples

stages.note: Four colossal seated statues of Ramesses II guard the temple entrance.
Drifting sand has buried much of the temple.
The temples were cut into blocks and moved to higher ground to save them from the rising waters of Lake Nasser.

fact: The Great Temple of Abu Simbel was carved into a sandstone cliff about 1264–1244 BCE. Twice a year, sunlight reaches deep inside to light up statues in the inner sanctuary.

name: Burj Khalifa
fact: Burj Khalifa in Dubai, finished in 2010, is about 828 m tall, the tallest building in the world.

name: Great Zimbabwe

stages.note: Great Zimbabwe is a busy capital and trade centre, linked to the Indian Ocean.
A World Heritage Site and a symbol of Zimbabwe, whose name means "houses of stone".

fact: Great Zimbabwe's Great Enclosure has walls up to 11 m high, built from granite blocks fitted together without mortar.

name: Djinguereber Mosque, Timbuktu

stages.note: The mosque is a centre of learning in one of Africa's great scholarly cities.
Townspeople re-plaster the mud walls together in an annual festival.

fact: Djinguereber Mosque in Timbuktu was built around 1327, during the reign of Mansa Musa of Mali. It is made of mud brick, straw and wood.
facts: Timbuktu's libraries hold hundreds of thousands of manuscripts on astronomy, mathematics, law and medicine.

name: Great Mosque of Djenné

stages.note: An early great mosque stands at the heart of the town.
The present mosque was rebuilt in 1907 and is the largest mud-brick building in the world.

fact: Each year the people of Djenné hold the Crépissage, a festival where everyone helps re-plaster the mosque with fresh mud.

name: Church of St George, Lalibela

stages.note: The church was carved downward from a single block of volcanic rock.

fact: The rock-hewn churches of Lalibela, in Ethiopia, were carved out of solid rock in the late 1100s and early 1200s, and are still used for worship.

name: Victoria Falls
fact: Victoria Falls, on the Zambezi River, is about 1.7 km wide. Its local name, Mosi-oa-Tunya, means "the smoke that thunders".

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
fact: Kilimanjaro, in Tanzania, is Africa's highest mountain at 5,895 m. It is a dormant volcano with glaciers near the equator.

name: Stonehenge

stages.note: A circular ditch and bank have been dug, and the first stones are arriving.
The great sarsen stones stand in a circle, aligned with the midsummer sunrise and midwinter sunset.

fact: Stonehenge was built in stages from about 3000 BCE. Its largest sarsen stones weigh around 25 tonnes.
facts: The smaller bluestones were brought about 250 km from the Preseli Hills in Wales.

name: Parthenon, Acropolis

stages.note: The Parthenon gleams with painted sculpture on top of the Acropolis.
An explosion in 1687 destroyed much of the roof and middle.
Careful restoration has been going on since the 1970s.

fact: The Parthenon was built in 447–432 BCE in honour of the goddess Athena. Its columns are slightly curved so that they look perfectly straight.

name: Colosseum

stages.note: Crowds of up to 50,000 gather in the amphitheatre.
An earthquake in 1349 brought down part of the outer wall.

fact: The Colosseum in Rome opened in 80 CE. It could hold around 50,000 people, who came and went through 80 numbered entrances.

name: Pantheon
fact: The Pantheon's dome, finished around 125 CE, is still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world. The round opening at its top, the oculus, is 8.2 m across.

name: Notre-Dame de Paris

stages.note: The cathedral is being built over many decades by stonemasons, carpenters and glassmakers.
A restoration led by Viollet-le-Duc added a new spire.
After a fire in 2019, craftspeople are rebuilding the roof and spire.
Notre-Dame reopened in December 2024.

fact: Notre-Dame de Paris is a masterpiece of Gothic architecture, famous for its flying buttresses, rose windows and gargoyles.

name: Eiffel Tower

stages.note: The tower opens for the 1889 World's Fair.

fact: The Eiffel Tower was built in 1887–1889. At 300 m it was the tallest structure in the world until 1930.
facts: It is held together by about 2.5 million rivets and is repainted every few years.

name: Elizabeth Tower (Big Ben)
fact: "Big Ben" is the name of the great bell inside the clock tower at Westminster. The tower was renamed Elizabeth Tower in 2012.

name: Leaning Tower of Pisa

stages.note: The tower began to lean while it was still being built.
Engineers reduced the lean so the tower would stay standing.

fact: The Leaning Tower of Pisa began to lean during construction because of soft ground on one side.

name: Neuschwanstein Castle
fact: Neuschwanstein, a 19th-century romantic castle in Bavaria, was built for King Ludwig II.

name: Sagrada Família

stages.note: Antoni Gaudí's basilica is slowly rising, funded by donations.
Imagined: the basilica is finally complete.

fact: Construction of the Sagrada Família in Barcelona began in 1882. Antoni Gaudí worked on it for over 40 years.

name: Brandenburg Gate
fact: The Brandenburg Gate in Berlin was completed in 1791, and has become a symbol of German reunification.

name: Mont-Saint-Michel
fact: Mont-Saint-Michel is a tidal island in Normandy crowned by an abbey. At high tide the sea can surround it.

name: Tower Bridge
fact: Tower Bridge in London, opened in 1894, has two halves (bascules) that lift to let tall ships pass.

name: Lascaux cave

stages.note: The cave is here, but its walls are still bare.
Ice Age artists have painted horses, aurochs and deer on the walls.
Teenagers rediscovered the cave in 1940. It has been closed since 1963 to protect the paintings.

fact: The Lascaux cave paintings, about 17,000 years old, show horses, aurochs, deer and other animals in red, yellow and black.

name: Taj Mahal
fact: The Taj Mahal in Agra was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. Its white marble is inlaid with semi-precious stones.

name: Qutub Minar
fact: Qutub Minar in Delhi, begun in 1199, is a 72.5 m tower of red sandstone and marble.

name: Great Stupa at Sanchi

stages.note: Carved stone gateways tell stories from the life of the Buddha.

fact: The Great Stupa at Sanchi was first built in the 3rd century BCE under the emperor Ashoka, and is one of the oldest stone structures in India.

name: Mount Everest
fact: Mount Everest, called Sagarmatha in Nepali and Chomolungma in Tibetan, is 8,849 m high, the highest point above sea level on Earth.
facts: Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary first reached the summit in 1953.

name: Great Wall at Badaling

stages.note: Earlier walls of rammed earth guard the northern frontier.
Ming dynasty builders have rebuilt the wall here in brick and stone.
The Badaling section was restored and opened to visitors.

fact: The Great Wall of China is not one wall but many, built and rebuilt over 2,000 years. The famous brick sections near Beijing are from the Ming dynasty.

name: Forbidden City

stages.note: The imperial palace is home to the emperor and his court.
The palace became the Palace Museum in 1925.

fact: The Forbidden City in Beijing was the imperial palace of the Ming and Qing dynasties. It has about 980 buildings, and its roofs are covered in yellow-glazed tiles.

name: Temple of Heaven

stages.note: The Hall of Prayer was rebuilt after a fire in 1889.

fact: At the Temple of Heaven in Beijing, emperors prayed for good harvests. The round Hall of Prayer stands on three marble terraces.

name: Himeji Castle
fact: Himeji Castle, completed in 1609, is called the "White Heron Castle" because of its brilliant white plaster walls.

name: Mount Fuji
fact: Mount Fuji, at 3,776 m, is Japan's highest mountain. It is an active volcano that last erupted in 1707.

name: Tokyo Tower
fact: Tokyo Tower, opened in 1958, is painted international orange and white for aviation safety.

name: Su Song's Astronomical Clock Tower

stages.note: Water drives a great wheel that turns a celestial globe and rings bells and drums every hour.
The clock tower was dismantled and taken away in 1127.

fact: Su Song's clock tower in Kaifeng, completed in 1092, was a water-powered astronomical clock with an escapement mechanism, centuries before Europe's mechanical clocks.

name: Angkor Wat

stages.note: Angkor Wat is the heart of the Khmer capital, built as a temple to Vishnu.

fact: Angkor Wat, built in the early 1100s, is the largest religious monument in the world. Its five towers represent the peaks of Mount Meru.

name: Borobudur

stages.note: The temple is covered by volcanic ash and jungle.
A great restoration finished in 1983.

fact: Borobudur in Java is the world's largest Buddhist temple. Its terraces hold 72 bell-shaped stupas and over 2,600 relief panels.

name: Petronas Towers
fact: The Petronas Towers in Kuala Lumpur were the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 to 2004. A skybridge links them.

name: Ha Long Bay
fact: Ha Long Bay in Vietnam has about 1,600 limestone islands and islets rising from emerald water.

name: Sydney Opera House
fact: The Sydney Opera House, opened in 1973, is roofed with shell-shaped vaults covered in over a million tiles.

name: Uluru
fact: Uluru is a giant sandstone monolith in central Australia, sacred to the Aṉangu people. It glows red at sunrise and sunset.

name: Great Barrier Reef
fact: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system, stretching over 2,300 km. It can be seen from space.

name: Moai of Ahu Tongariki

stages.note: The moai face inland, watching over the community.
By the 1800s all the moai on Rapa Nui had been toppled.
The 15 moai of Ahu Tongariki were re-erected in the 1990s.

fact: The moai of Rapa Nui (Easter Island) were carved from volcanic tuff, mostly between about 1250 and 1500, to honour ancestors.

name: Statue of Liberty

stages.note: The new statue gleams copper-brown.
The copper has turned green with a protective patina.

fact: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from the people of France to the United States, dedicated in 1886. Its copper skin is only about 2.4 mm thick.

name: Grand Canyon
fact: The Grand Canyon, carved by the Colorado River, is up to 1.8 km deep. Its rock layers record nearly two billion years of Earth's history.

name: Golden Gate Bridge
fact: The Golden Gate Bridge opened in 1937. Its colour, "International Orange", was chosen to stand out in the fog.

name: Empire State Building
fact: The Empire State Building was built in just 410 days and opened in 1931. It was the world's tallest building for nearly 40 years.

name: CN Tower
fact: Toronto's CN Tower, 553 m tall, was the world's tallest free-standing structure from 1976 to 2007.

name: Monks Mound, Cahokia

stages.note: Cahokia is a large city with plazas, mounds and a wooden palisade.

fact: Monks Mound at Cahokia is the largest earthen mound in the Americas, built by Mississippian people around 900–1200 CE.

name: Cliff Palace, Mesa Verde

stages.note: The Ancestral Puebloans moved away around 1300.

fact: Cliff Palace in Mesa Verde, with about 150 rooms, is the largest cliff dwelling in North America, built by Ancestral Puebloans.

name: Pueblo Bonito, Chaco Canyon
fact: Pueblo Bonito was a great house with about 600 rooms, up to four storeys high, at the centre of the Chaco world.

name: Niagara Falls
fact: Niagara Falls formed at the end of the last ice age, about 12,000 years ago. The Horseshoe Falls drop about 51 m.

name: Launch Complex 39A

stages.note: A Saturn V rocket stands on the launch pad.

fact: Apollo 11 launched from Launch Complex 39A in Florida on 16 July 1969, carrying Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins.

name: El Castillo, Chichén Itzá

stages.note: The jungle has grown over the city.

fact: El Castillo has four staircases of 91 steps. With the top platform they make 365, one for each day of the year. At the equinoxes, shadows form a serpent on its stairs.

name: Pyramid of the Sun, Teotihuacan

stages.note: Teotihuacan is one of the largest cities in the world, painted in bright colours.

fact: The Pyramid of the Sun at Teotihuacan is one of the largest pyramids in the world. It lies along the Avenue of the Dead.

name: Temple I, Tikal

stages.note: Tikal has been abandoned to the rainforest.

fact: Temple I at Tikal, in Guatemala, rises 47 m above the rainforest and was built around 732 CE.

name: Machu Picchu

stages.note: Machu Picchu is a royal estate of the Inca emperor Pachacuti.
Machu Picchu has been left behind and is slowly being overgrown.

fact: Machu Picchu was built around 1450 high in the Andes. Its stones are cut so precisely that they fit together without mortar.

name: Christ the Redeemer
fact: Christ the Redeemer, 30 m tall, stands on Corcovado mountain above Rio de Janeiro. Its arms stretch 28 m wide.

name: Nazca Lines
fact: The Nazca Lines are giant figures and lines scraped into the desert of Peru between about 500 BCE and 500 CE. Many are best seen from the air.

name: Svalbard Global Seed Vault
fact: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault, opened in 2008, stores backup copies of seeds from crops all over the world, deep in the permafrost.

name: Mount Erebus
fact: Mount Erebus, in Antarctica, is the southernmost active volcano on Earth and has a long-lived lava lake.

name: Archive of Anywhen

stages.note: The Archive of Anywhen, home of the Time Walkers.

fact: Imagined: the Archive of Anywhen is where every moment of history is studied and cared for. It was built near where the Library of Alexandria once stood.

name: Rainhill Trials track

stages.note: The track is ready for the locomotive trials.
The Liverpool and Manchester Railway is open.

fact: The Rainhill Trials of October 1829 tested locomotives for the Liverpool and Manchester Railway. Stephenson's Rocket reached about 48 km/h.

name: Tranquility Base

stages.note: The Apollo 11 lunar module descent stage, a flag and footprints remain.

fact: Apollo 11's lunar module Eagle landed in the Sea of Tranquility on 20 July 1969. Its descent stage is still there.
